images.title: Dividing by ten each step
images.purpose: Show the next place after hundredths: splitting by 10 again gives thousandths, and each step to the right divides by 10.
images.composition: Four boxes in a row, shrinking from left to right, joined by three arrows; plenty of white space above and below.
exact_structure: Four squares in one row from left to right, each clearly smaller than the one before.

Square 1 is teal (#0072B2) labelled 1. Square 2 is amber (#E69F00) labelled 1/10. Square 3 is green (#009E73) labelled 1/100. Square 4 is reddish purple (#CC79A7) labelled 1/1000, the focus, with a thick outline.
Three grey (#6B7280) right pointing arrows between the squares, each labelled ÷ 10.
Under square 4 the words one thousandth. A caption below the row: 1000 of these make 1.
rejection: fewer or more than 4 squares or 3 arrows
squares not shrinking left to right
any label other than the listed fractions
any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Each step to the right divides by 10, and the fourth step gives one thousandth.
images.description: A row of four shrinking squares labelled 1, 1/10, 1/100 and 1/1000 with divide by ten arrows between them.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Follow the arrows and say what each new part is.

image_decisions.why: The chain shows how thousandths follow from hundredths and why the system is called decimal.
